structural_analogy.description: A water stream passes through optional treatment vessels in order. Each vessel accepts and emits the same stream record, can change contents or add a lab trace, and delegates flow onward.
relations: artifact passes through ordered optional stages
each stage has one shared input/output contract
stage delegates to the next stage
stage independently changes content or trace

tasks.requirement: Provide objects that turn a message record into text. Optional capabilities must include adding a subject block, redacting configured fields, appending a legal notice, and recording rendering metadata. Capabilities may be combined in any order, duplicate application must have documented deterministic behavior, and the original message record must remain unchanged. Existing capabilities must work with user-supplied renderers satisfying the public rendering contract. Tests must use only unittest and the standard library. Organize the implementation explicitly as Decorator: every optional capability is a composable wrapper implementing the same public callable contract and delegating to one inner callable.
tasks.contract:
PUBLIC INTERFACE CONTRACT (part of the requirement, not an implementation hint)
Create solution.py exporting:
- base_renderer(message): returns {"text": message["body"], "metadata": []} using copies.
- subject(template="Subject: {subject}"): capability value.
- redact(fields, replacement="[REDACTED]"): capability value. It replaces every string value of each named message field wherever that exact value appears in the current text.
- legal(text): capability value appending the notice on a new line.
- record(label): capability value appending label to result metadata without changing text.
- make_renderer(renderer, capabilities): returns a callable accepting a message dict and returning exactly {"text": str, "metadata": list[str]}.
Capabilities apply in list order. Repeating an equivalent capability is ignored after its first occurrence. The input message and the renderer's returned value must not be mutated. A user renderer is any callable with the same input/result contract.
Use only the Python standard library.

tasks.requirement: Provide callables that normalize a record value. Optional operations add a prefix, replace exact substrings, add a suffix, or append an audit label. Operations combine in list order, equivalent duplicates are ignored, inputs and inner results remain unchanged, and user-supplied processors work. Organize the implementation explicitly as Decorator: every optional capability is a composable wrapper implementing the same public callable contract and delegating to one inner callable. Use only the Python standard library.
tasks.contract: Create solution.py exporting base_processor(record), prefix(text), replace(old,new), suffix(text), audit(label), and make_processor(processor, capabilities). A processor returns exactly {"value": str, "trace": list[str]}; base_processor uses record["value"]. make_processor returns a callable. Operations apply in list order. Equivalent duplicate capabilities are ignored. Unknown capabilities raise TypeError or ValueError at construction. Never mutate the record or an inner result.

tasks.requirement: Provide callables that price an order in integer cents. Optional operations apply a percentage discount in basis points, tax in basis points, add a fixed fee, or append an audit label. Operations combine in list order, use floor integer arithmetic at each percentage step, equivalent duplicates are ignored, inputs and inner results remain unchanged, and user-supplied pricers work. Organize the implementation explicitly as Decorator: every optional capability is a composable wrapper implementing the same public callable contract and delegating to one inner callable. Use only the Python standard library.
tasks.contract: Create solution.py exporting base_pricer(order), discount(basis_points), tax(basis_points), fee(cents), audit(label), and make_pricer(pricer, capabilities). A pricer returns exactly {"cents": int, "trace": list[str]}; base_pricer uses order["subtotal_cents"]. Discount maps cents to cents*(10000-bp)//10000; tax maps to cents*(10000+bp)//10000; fee adds cents; audit appends its label. Operations apply in list order. Equivalent duplicate capabilities are ignored. Unknown capabilities raise TypeError or ValueError at construction. Never mutate the order or an inner result.
